definitions.explanation: Literally having the smell of mud or earth, as with freshwater fish or unwashed vegetables.

definitions.gloss: unrefined; rustic; unsophisticated; rough around the edges
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, lacking polish or elegance. Can be used critically to mean crude, or positively to mean earnest and down-to-earth.

examples.japanese: この{魚|さかな}は{泥臭|どろくさ}い。
{川|かわ}で{釣|つ}った{魚|さかな}は{泥臭|どろくさ}いことがある。
examples.english: Fish caught in rivers can sometimes have a muddy smell.

examples.japanese: {泥臭|どろくさ}さを{取|と}るために{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}に{漬|つ}けておく。
examples.english: Soak it in milk to remove the muddy smell.

examples.japanese: {泥臭|どろくさ}いやり{方|かた}だ。
examples.english: It's an unrefined way of doing things.

examples.japanese: {泥臭|どろくさ}い{営業|えいぎょう}スタイルが{彼|かれ}の{持|も}ち{味|あじ}だ。
examples.english: His gritty sales style is his strong point.

examples.japanese: スマートではないが、{泥臭|どろくさ}い{努力|どりょく}が{最後|さいご}には{実|みの}を{結|むす}んだ。
examples.english: It wasn't elegant, but the unglamorous hard work bore fruit in the end.

notes:
USAGE:
{泥臭|どろくさ}い is an i-adjective combining {泥|どろ} (mud) and {臭|くさ}い (smelling of). The figurative sense (sense 2) can be either negative (crude, unsophisticated) or positive (earnest, gritty, down-to-earth), depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {泥臭|どろくさ}い{努力|どりょく} (unglamorous effort)
- {泥臭|どろくさ}いやり{方|かた} (rough-and-ready approach)
- {泥臭|どろくさ}い{営業|えいぎょう} (gritty salesmanship)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{野暮|やぼ}ったい means unfashionable or unsophisticated in appearance or taste. {泥臭|どろくさ}い emphasizes a raw, unpolished quality that can imply hard work and persistence.
